statement: Convert a mesh into a mesh graph in which faces are nodes and shared edges are links, carrying per-face and per-edge data containers alongside the geometry.
superiority: Dino 8 should keep a native face-adjacency graph on every mesh with attribute channels, so graph queries need no conversion step.

acceptance.corpus: Icosphere with 20 480 faces and a cube with 12 triangles
acceptance.tolerance: Node count equals face count; link count equals interior edge count (E_int = 3F/2 for closed triangle meshes) exactly

statement: Analyze a mesh through its face graph: traverse adjacency, find connected regions and compute graph distances between faces.
superiority: Dino 8 should run adjacency queries in parallel with deterministic ordering and handle million-face meshes interactively.

acceptance.corpus: Mesh with 3 disconnected shells of known sizes
acceptance.tolerance: Connected-region count = 3 and each size exact; shortest face-path length equals BFS reference on 100 random pairs

notes: The McNeel announcement page describes analysis and partitioning but does not list individual component names.

statement: Partition a mesh into patches of connected faces based on graph criteria so each patch can be processed or fabricated separately.
superiority: Dino 8 should offer partitions with developability and size limits and explain why a patch was split.

acceptance.corpus: Sphere mesh partitioned into patches with max 50 faces
acceptance.tolerance: Every face in exactly one patch; each patch connected; no patch exceeds 50 faces

statement: Unroll an unstructured triangle mesh into flat pieces, keeping edge lengths, optionally adding glue flaps, numbering text identifiers and separate fold-in and fold-out score lines for assembly.
superiority: Dino 8 should unroll meshes with holes and branching reliably, report per-piece distortion and produce cut-ready files with nesting.

acceptance.corpus: Developable triangulated cylinder and a cone
acceptance.tolerance: Flat edge lengths equal 3D edge lengths within 1e-6; piece areas preserved within 1e-6

acceptance.corpus: Mesh with triangular openings (case that fails in the original)
acceptance.tolerance: Unroll succeeds or returns a clear diagnostic, never silent failure

notes: Forum threads record unroll failures when holes are present and outputs hidden by default; Dino 8 should avoid both.

statement: Prepare a surface for mesh-graph work by converting it to a mesh with controlled face size and quality.

source.ref: Surface to mesh preparation for Ivy

superiority: Dino 8 should remesh to a target edge length and report triangle quality metrics before unrolling.

acceptance.corpus: Freeform surface meshed to 20 mm edge length
acceptance.tolerance: Edge lengths within 20 percent of target; min angle >= 20 degrees on 99 percent of faces

notes: Forum reply recommends meshing surfaces before use with Ivy; no dedicated component was confirmed.
